# Beat and pitch analysis

*To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_analysis](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_analysis) starting point.*

Where the beats are and what note is sounding are separate questions here, and they arrive as
separate jobs. `analysis.beats` takes the first at several window lengths at once, since a tempo
figure means little apart from the window it was measured over. For the second, how much is
sounding at once decides: `analysis.pitch_mono` tracks one voice as a continuous F0 with a voicing
probability, and `analysis.pitch_poly` returns discrete note events and a MIDI file where there are
chords.

| Field operation | Implementation | What comes back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `analysis.beats` | librosa beat tracking and multi-window tempograms | onset envelope, beat markers, local BPM and confidence at every requested scale |
| `analysis.pitch_mono` | librosa pYIN | monophonic F0, MIDI pitch, voiced flag and voiced probability |
| `analysis.pitch_poly` | Spotify Basic Pitch | note events, activation tensors, pitch bends and a MIDI artifact |

All three are durable, cached jobs on the same machinery as generation, and each asks for one
result rather than a family of candidates: a fixed window with fixed parameters has a single
answer, so there is nothing here to browse by seed. A request names an exact `AssetRegion` and the
recording on disk is never modified. Progress arrives on the WebSocket and in the embedded job
monitor, and the finished job points at a compressed NPZ asset instead of putting a large tensor
into Field's output JSON.

## The views

Every panel draws a preview the server has downsampled; the full-resolution arrays stay in the
NPZ asset. The beat view separates onset, tempo and confidence lanes; pYIN
shows pitch against a note grid with its voicing track; Basic Pitch combines a piano roll with
maximum activation and active-pitch count.
Hover, zoom and pan one panel and the others follow. A live board can join the source player on the
same shared timeline: playback drives every analysis cursor, hovering either surface highlights the
other, and clicking an analysis plot seeks the recording.

## Running all three from one box

The source waveform appears immediately. The persistent monitor and three replace-in-place status
cards report each job while the worker runs, and a job becomes a panel on the analysis board only
once it has finished successfully.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture

val client = FieldAudioClient()
val start = 18.0
val duration = 24.0
val timeSync = "nancy-analysis"
display("all jobs", fieldAudioJobMonitor(heightPixels = 330))

client.assetByFilename("*Nancy*").thenCompose { source ->
    val region = AssetRegion(source.id, start, duration)
    val canonical = source.representations.first { it.role == "canonical_project" }
    display("source", canonical.audioVisualizerHtml(
        label = "Nancy · 18–42 s",
        options = AudioVisualizerOptions(
            initialStartSeconds = start,
            initialDurationSeconds = duration,
            initialPositionSeconds = start,
            syncGroup = timeSync,
        ),
    ))

    val requests = [
        "beats" to multiScaleBeatAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
        "monophonic pitch" to monophonicPitchAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
        "polyphonic pitch" to polyphonicPitchAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
    ]
    val futures = requests.map { (label, request) ->
        client.submit(request).thenCompose { accepted ->
            display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted))
            client.watch(accepted.jobId) { event ->
                display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted, event))
            }
            client.awaitAnalysis(accepted)
        }
    }
    CompletableFuture.allOf(*futures.toTypedArray()).thenApply {
        futures.map { it.join() }
    }
}.thenAccept { results ->
    display("analysis", analysisDashboardHtml(
        results, panelHeight = 250,
        syncGroup = timeSync, timeOffsetSeconds = start,
    ))
}.exceptionally { error ->
    display("analysis error", error.cause?.message ?: error.message ?: error.toString())
    null
}
```

An unchanged request still goes through `submit` and `awaitAnalysis`, but the service resolves it to
the content-addressed cached result. Change the source range or an algorithm parameter to create a
new operation. `AnalysisResult.data` is the complete NPZ representation;
`AnalysisResult.artifacts` includes Basic Pitch MIDI where applicable; `client.download(...)`
copies either immutable asset when local numerical work needs the full resolution.

See also the [general audio visualizers](visualizers.md#beat-and-pitch-analysis-views), the
[gesture board](audio_ai_gesture_board.md) and [speech embeddings](audio_ai_speech_embeddings.md).

import java.util.concurrent.CancellationException
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture

val client = cached { FieldAudioClient() }
val start = 18.0
val duration = 24.0
val timeSync = "nancy-analysis"
display("all jobs", fieldAudioJobMonitor(heightPixels = 330))

runAsync(
    onResult = { results: List<AnalysisResult> ->
        display(
            "analysis",
            analysisDashboardHtml(
                results,
                panelHeight = 250,
                syncGroup = timeSync,
                timeOffsetSeconds = start,
            ),
        )
    },

    },

    val showSource = progress<String> { display("source", it) }

    val run = RunScope.current()
    val lookup = client.assetByFilename("*Nancy*")
    onCancel { lookup.cancel(true) }
    lookup.thenCompose { source ->
        if (future.isDone) throw CancellationException("run ended")

        val region = AssetRegion(source.id, start, duration)
        val canonical = source.representations.firstOrNull { it.role == "canonical_project" }
            ?: source.representations.first { it.mediaType in ["audio/wav", "audio/x-wav"] }
        showSource(
            canonical.audioVisualizerHtml(
                label = "Nancy · 18–42 s",
                options = AudioVisualizerOptions(
                    initialStartSeconds = start,
                    initialDurationSeconds = duration,
                    initialPositionSeconds = start,
                    syncGroup = timeSync,
                ),
            ),

            "beats" to multiScaleBeatAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
            "monophonic pitch" to monophonicPitchAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
            "polyphonic pitch" to polyphonicPitchAnalysis(region, requestedBy = "field:analysis-example"),
        ]
        val analyses = requests.map { (label, request) ->
            RunScope.withCurrent(run) {
                    client.trackAnalysis(
                        request,
                        onAccepted = { display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(it)) },
                        onProgress = { job, event -> display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(job, event)) },
                        onCompleted = { display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(it)) },
                        onError = {}, // The outer operation reports failure once.
                    )
                }
                .also { pending -> onCancel { pending.cancel(true) } }
        }
        CompletableFuture.allOf(*analyses.toTypedArray()).thenApply { analyses.map { it.join() } }
    }
}
```

An unchanged request still goes through `trackAnalysis`, but the service resolves it to
the content-addressed cached result. Change the source range or an algorithm parameter to create a
new operation. Stop or rerun closes this run’s progress subscriptions and suppresses stale output;
the durable service jobs and their cached results remain available. `AnalysisResult.data` is the complete NPZ representation;

copies either immutable asset when local numerical work needs the full resolution.

# Short-time spectral spaces

*To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_spectral_embeddings](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_spectral_embeddings) starting point.*

A resonance sliding upward, a hiss that thickens, a room closing in around a voice: none of that
needs a trained model to notice, only a record of which frequencies are loud from one moment to the
next. `analysis.embed_spectral` keeps that record as mel bands, log-mel bands and MFCCs, and Field
lays the frames out as a map you can play through.

```diffstatic_runner {data-lang=kotlin screenshot="assets/audio_ai_spectral_embeddings/spectral_spaces.png" capture="box" open-outputs="true" wait="4" padding="16" timeout="180" w="1120" h="1100" hidden=true embed=true name="elsewhere-spectral" alt="Three real Field t-SNE projections of librosa mel, log-mel and MFCC frames"}
:::static
import afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayLoader
import java.io.File
import java.nio.file.Path
val json = FieldAudioClient.json
val folder = File("public/docs/assets/audio_ai_spectral_embeddings")
val preview = json.decodeFromString<AnalysisPreview>(File(folder, "result-preview.json").readText())
val frames = decodeSpectralEmbeddingMessagePack(File(folder, "frames.msgpack").readBytes(), maxFrames = 600, durationSeconds = 10.0, poolMillis = 200.0, hopMillis = 40.0)
val previews = [SpectralEmbeddingDistance.MEL_WASSERSTEIN, SpectralEmbeddingDistance.LOG_MEL_COSINE, SpectralEmbeddingDistance.MFCC_EUCLIDEAN].mapIndexed { index, distance ->
    preview.withSpectralProjection(frames.tsne(dimensions = 4, distance = distance, perplexity = 30.0, maxIterations = 750, seed = 184921L + index))
}
display("spectral spaces", spectralEmbeddingPreviewDashboardHtml(previews, width = 1040, phaseHeight = 210))

```

Three distances give three views of the first ten seconds of `near_drowning.wav`: mel transport,
log-mel cosine and MFCC Euclidean. Each projection is computed by Field from the worker's real
spectral frames.

One cached librosa job holds all three representations. How much audio pools into one point,
which distance compares two points, and whether MDS or t-SNE lays them out are all chosen in
Field afterwards, so changing them does not analyse the sound again.

The retained representations follow librosa's
[mel-spectrogram](https://librosa.org/doc/latest/generated/librosa.feature.melspectrogram.html) and
[MFCC](https://librosa.org/doc/main/api/generated/librosa.feature.mfcc.html) definitions. “Earth mover”
here is one-dimensional [Wasserstein-1 distance](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance.html)
across the mel bands.

For maps built from trained speech models (WavLM, emotion2vec), see
[speech-reactive spaces](audio_ai_speech_embeddings.md). The spectral maps answer simpler questions:
where the energy is, and how the spectral envelope changes.

| Field distance | Representation | What proximity tends to mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MEL_WASSERSTEIN` | per-frame unit-mass mel spectrum | little spectral mass must move far along the perceptual frequency axis |
| `LOG_MEL_COSINE` | 64 absolute log-mel bands | similar spectral-envelope direction, relatively insensitive to overall scale |
| `LOG_MEL_EUCLIDEAN` | 64 absolute log-mel bands | similar absolute band-energy pattern, including level |
| `MFCC_COSINE` | 20 cepstral coefficients | similar compact envelope/timbre direction |
| `MFCC_EUCLIDEAN` | 20 cepstral coefficients | similar compact envelope/timbre and coefficient magnitude |

Which row to reach for depends on what is moving. Mel Wasserstein is especially useful when a
formant, resonant background sound, or spectral emphasis slides in frequency: it charges in
proportion to how far mass moves. MFCCs suppress fine spectral detail and make broad envelope
changes easier to see. Log-mel retains the most directly inspectable band structure.

## Plotting a recording

This box finds the already imported `near_drowning.wav` or imports it, displays the source, submits
and monitors one durable analysis job, downloads the artifact, and compares three t-SNE readings of
the first ten seconds. Every panel shares the source player's cursor in both directions.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
import afield.document.graph.Box
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Path
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture

geometry have no stable meaning. Either algorithm can use any of the distances above, including

# Short-time spectral spaces

*To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_spectral_embeddings](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_spectral_embeddings) starting point.*

A resonance sliding upward, a hiss that thickens, a room closing in around a voice: none of that
needs a trained model to notice, only a record of which frequencies are loud from one moment to the
next. `analysis.embed_spectral` keeps that record as mel bands, log-mel bands and MFCCs, and Field
lays the frames out as a map you can play through.

Three distances give three views of the first ten seconds of `near_drowning.wav`: mel transport,
log-mel cosine and MFCC Euclidean. Each projection is computed by Field from the worker's real
spectral frames.

One cached librosa job holds all three representations. How much audio pools into one point,
which distance compares two points, and whether MDS or t-SNE lays them out are all chosen in
Field afterwards, so changing them does not analyse the sound again.

The retained representations follow librosa's
[mel-spectrogram](https://librosa.org/doc/latest/generated/librosa.feature.melspectrogram.html) and
[MFCC](https://librosa.org/doc/main/api/generated/librosa.feature.mfcc.html) definitions. “Earth mover”
here is one-dimensional [Wasserstein-1 distance](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance.html)
across the mel bands.

For maps built from trained speech models (WavLM, emotion2vec), see
[speech-reactive spaces](audio_ai_speech_embeddings.md). The spectral maps answer simpler questions:
where the energy is, and how the spectral envelope changes.

| Field distance | Representation | What proximity tends to mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MEL_WASSERSTEIN` | per-frame unit-mass mel spectrum | little spectral mass must move far along the perceptual frequency axis |
| `LOG_MEL_COSINE` | 64 absolute log-mel bands | similar spectral-envelope direction, relatively insensitive to overall scale |
| `LOG_MEL_EUCLIDEAN` | 64 absolute log-mel bands | similar absolute band-energy pattern, including level |
| `MFCC_COSINE` | 20 cepstral coefficients | similar compact envelope/timbre direction |
| `MFCC_EUCLIDEAN` | 20 cepstral coefficients | similar compact envelope/timbre and coefficient magnitude |

Which row to reach for depends on what is moving. Mel Wasserstein is especially useful when a
formant, resonant background sound, or spectral emphasis slides in frequency: it charges in
proportion to how far mass moves. MFCCs suppress fine spectral detail and make broad envelope
changes easier to see. Log-mel retains the most directly inspectable band structure.

# Corpus microscope: from recordings to related windows

*To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_corpus_microscope](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_corpus_microscope) starting point.*

The corpus microscope finds the stretches of a set of recordings that sound most like a passage you
pick. It first cuts every recording into overlapping windows of 1.5, 3, 6 and 12 seconds and
measures each one; the audio files themselves are left unchanged. Distance is made of five
measurements (harmony, pitch, texture, rhythm and dynamics), and you choose how much each one
counts. The examples here query six seconds of Nancy against Final Out at Candlestick Park.

```diffstatic_runner {data-lang=kotlin screenshot="assets/audio_ai_corpus_microscope/neighbours.png" capture="box" open-outputs="true" wait="4" padding="16" timeout="180" w="1120" h="1100" hidden=true embed=true name="elsewhere-corpus" alt="Real Nancy query and two Candlestick neighbour windows with waveforms, distance bars and splice players" capture-profile="linux-nvidia"}

import afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayLoader
import java.io.File
import java.nio.file.Path
val json = FieldAudioClient.json
val folder = File("public/docs/assets/audio_ai_corpus_microscope")

```

separate distances for harmony, pitch, texture, rhythm and dynamics.

## What each window is measured by

| Group | Measurements |
| --- | --- |
| harmony | mean and variation of twelve chroma classes |
| pitch | dominant-pitch centre, spread and voiced fraction |
| texture | MFCC plus spectral centroid, bandwidth, flatness and rolloff |
| rhythm | onset strength, peak density and local tempo statistics |
| dynamics | RMS centre, spread and range |

Each group is pooled over the window, and the five together are the vector a query is matched
against.

## Submit and monitor the index

Segmentation and descriptor extraction are ordinary cached `analysis.*` jobs. This box indexes Nancy and Final Out at Candlestick Park:

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture

val client = FieldAudioClient()
display("all jobs", fieldAudioJobMonitor(heightPixels = 330))

fun tracked(label: String, operation: ModelOperation): CompletableFuture<AnalysisResult> =
    client.submit(operation).thenCompose { accepted ->
        display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted))
        client.watch(accepted.jobId) { event ->
            display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted, event))
        }
        client.awaitAnalysis(accepted)
    }

val lookups = ["*Nancy*", "*Candlestick Park*"].map { client.assetByFilename(it) }
CompletableFuture.allOf(*lookups.toTypedArray()).thenCompose {
    val assets = lookups.map { it.join() }
    val jobs = assets.map { asset ->
        val whole = AssetRegion(asset.id, 0.0, requireNotNull(asset.durationSeconds))
        tracked("segments", segmentCorpus(whole, requestedBy = "field:corpus/index"))
            .thenCompose {
                tracked("descriptors", embedCorpus(whole, requestedBy = "field:corpus/index"))
            }
    }
    CompletableFuture.allOf(*jobs.toTypedArray()).thenApply { assets.first() }
}
```

`segmentCorpus` records deterministic windows and their previous/next source neighbours.
`embedCorpus` pools the five descriptor groups over those exact windows. Re-running either unchanged
request returns its saved result immediately.

## Query, await and visualize

A query is a job too, since the query passage has to be measured. Once it completes,
`corpusPreview` loads the neighbours and `corpusMicroscopeHtml` shows them with players you can
listen to. This query leaves out Nancy itself, so every result comes from Candlestick; set

        texture = 1.35,
        rhythm = 0.7,

Each neighbour card shows where the window comes from, a bar for each of the five distances, and a
player that crossfades from the query into the neighbour. The query and neighbour players both start

                    tracked(
                            run,
                            "source ${index + 1} descriptors",
                            embedCorpus(whole, requestedBy = "field:corpus/index"),
                        )
                        .also { pending -> onCancel { pending.cancel(true) } }
                }
        }
        CompletableFuture.allOf(*jobs.toTypedArray()).thenApply { assets.first() }
    }
}
```

`segmentCorpus` records deterministic windows and their previous/next source neighbours.
`embedCorpus` pools the five descriptor groups over those exact windows. Re-running either unchanged
request returns its saved result immediately.

## Query, await and visualize

A query is a job too, since the query passage has to be measured. Once it completes,
`corpusPreview` loads the neighbours and `corpusMicroscopeHtml` shows them with players you can
listen to. This query leaves out Nancy itself, so every result comes from Candlestick; set
`includeSameAsset = true` to search the query's own recording as well:

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val query = AssetRegion(nancy.id, startSeconds = 18.0, durationSeconds = 6.0)

runAsync<CorpusPreview>(
    onResult = { result ->
        preview = result
        canonical = nancy.representations.firstOrNull { it.role == "canonical_project" }
            ?: nancy.representations.first { it.mediaType in ["audio/wav", "audio/x-wav"] }
        display("microscope", corpusMicroscopeHtml(preview, canonical))
    },
    onError = { failure -> markdown("query error", "Query failed: ${(failure.message ?: failure.toString()).md}") },
) {
    val run = RunScope.current()
    val neighbours = tracked(
        run,
        "Nancy neighbours",
        findCorpusNeighbours(
            query,
            limit = 12,
            includeSameAsset = false,
            weights = CorpusDistanceWeights(
                harmony = 0.8,
                pitch = 0.55,
                texture = 1.35,
                rhythm = 0.7,
                dynamics = 0.35,
            ),
            requestedBy = "field:corpus/query",
        ),
    )
    onCancel { neighbours.cancel(true) }
    neighbours.thenCompose { result ->
        if (future.isDone) throw CancellationException("run ended")
        client.corpusPreview(result.id).also { pending -> onCancel { pending.cancel(true) } }
    }
}
```

Each neighbour card shows where the window comes from, a bar for each of the five distances, and a
player that crossfades from the query into the neighbour. The query and neighbour players both start
at zero, so hovering, zooming, clicking and playback stay aligned between the two recordings. Each
card also lists the window's timestamps in its source and the ids of the windows before and after
it.

## Place a neighbour as a box

Show the microscope with `showCorpusMicroscope` instead of `display`, and every neighbour card gets a
**place** button. Run this fragment after the query has produced its microscope. Pressing it makes a new box beside this one, named after the recording and the
window, whose code plays that window. It is ordinary box code: edit the times to move or stretch the
window, then run it.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
showCorpusMicroscope(preview, canonical)
```

`placeCorpusNeighbour(neighbour)` does the same from code. This box places the first neighbour and
shows the code the new box was given:

```diffstatic_runner {data-lang=kotlin screenshot="assets/audio_ai_corpus_microscope/placed.png" capture="box" open-outputs="true" wait="2" padding="16" timeout="120" w="900" h="260" embed=true name="corpus-placed" alt="The code of a box placed from the corpus microscope: a comment naming Final Out at Candlestick Park from 21.00 to 27.00 seconds, a corpusClip call for that window, and audio(clip.sampler())"}
:::static
import java.io.File

val folder = File("public/docs/assets/audio_ai_corpus_microscope")
val preview = FieldAudioClient.json.decodeFromString<CorpusPreview>(File(folder, "corpus.json").readText())
:::fold show the placed box's name and code
val placed = placeCorpusNeighbour(preview.neighbours.first())
markdown("placed", "**${placed.name}**\n\n```kotlin\n${placed.properties["code"]}```")
```

`corpusClip` fetches the recording from the Field audio service once, keeps it under
`~/.afield/cache/field-audio`, and cuts out the window; `clip.sampler()` plays it from the start.
